stem: Fill in the blank: ______ reactions never go for completion.
Fill in the blank: At equilibrium stage, the rate of forward reaction is ______ to the rate of backward reaction.
Fill in the blank: The equilibrium established in physical processes is called ______.
Fill in the blank: Equilibrium state is not static but ______ in nature.
Fill in the blank: On changing the temperature ______ state is disturbed.
True or false: Equilibrium reactions can take place only in closed vessels.
True or false: The equilibrium state can be attained from both sides of the chemical reaction.
True or false: A reaction continues even after the attainment of equilibrium.
True or false: The concentrations of reactants and products become equal when equilibrium is attained.
True or false: The properties of the system become constant at equilibrium and remain unchanged thereafter.
Classify as physical or chemical equilibrium: H 2 O(s) ⇌ H 2 O(l)
Classify as physical or chemical equilibrium: NH 4 Cl(s) ⇌ NH 4 Cl(l)
Classify as physical or chemical equilibrium: H 2 (g) + I 2 (g) ⇌ 2HI(g)
Classify as physical or chemical equilibrium: CaCO 3 (s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO 2 (g)
Which of the following symbols is used to represent a reversible reaction? (a) → (b) ⇌ (c) two stacked one-way arrows (d) ←

Which of the following statement is true for all reversible reactions? (a) They always proceed to completion (b) They can be started only from reactant side (c) They never attain equilibrium (d) They are never complete

In a closed container, liquid water and its vapour coexist at a fixed temperature. After some time, no observable change occurs. Which type of equilibrium is established? (a) Chemical equilibrium (b) Physical equilibrium (c) Homogeneous chemical equilibrium (d) Irreversible equilibrium

key: (c) Reversible reactions contain both reactants and products at equilibrium
stem: Which observation most clearly distinguishes a reversible reaction from an irreversible reaction? (a) Reversible reactions are faster (b) Irreversible reactions attain equilibrium (c) Reversible reactions contain both reactants and products at equilibrium (d) Irreversible reactions occur only in closed vessels

key: (a), (c), (d) macroscopic properties constant; opposing processes needed; balance from continuous activity
stem: Which of the following statement(s) are correct regarding equilibrium? [MULTIPLE CORRECT] (a) At equilibrium, macroscopic properties remain constant (b) At equilibrium, microscopic processes stop completely (c) Equilibrium can be established only when opposing processes occur (d) Equilibrium represents a balance achieved by continuous activity
Define irreversible chemical reaction.
Give examples of natural irreversible processes.
Define reversible chemical reaction.
Explain irreversible reaction with examples.

What type of reaction is characterized by the formation of an equilibrium state with both reactants and products present? (a) Irreversible Reaction (b) Combustion Reaction (c) Reversible Reaction (d) Precipitation Reaction

Which of the following is a correct characteristic of irreversible reactions? (a) They can proceed in both directions (b) They never reach equilibrium (c) Reactants are never fully converted (d) Represented with a reversible arrow
In which type of equilibrium is the physical state of the system changed without any chemical transformation? (a) Heterogeneous (b) Physical Equilibrium (c) Homogeneous (d) Chemical Equilibrium
What is the condition for a system to attain dynamic equilibrium? (a) Forward rate = 0 (b) Backward rate = 0 (c) Forward rate = Backward rate (d) Reactants = Products
Which process is NOT an example of physical equilibrium? (a) Fusion of ice (b) Evaporation of water (c) Precipitation reaction (d) Sublimation of iodine

A closed container at a fixed temperature contains water and its vapour. Initially the vapour pressure increases rapidly, then the rate of increase slows, and finally the vapour pressure becomes constant. Which statement best explains the constant vapour pressure stage? (a) Evaporation has stopped completely (b) Evaporation rate equals condensation rate (c) Vapour molecules no longer collide with the liquid surface (d) Condensation rate exceeds evaporation rate

key: (b) Condensation rate increases until equilibrium is restored ⚠
stem: In a closed vessel at constant temperature, solid iodine sublimes to give violet vapours until the vapour intensity becomes constant. If some vapour is suddenly removed, what will happen next? (a) Sublimation stops and condensation continues (b) Condensation rate increases until equilibrium is restored (c) Sublimation rate increases until equilibrium is restored (d) Both sublimation and condensation stop immediately

key: (b) Concentrations stop changing, but rates remain equal and non-zero
stem: In the graph of rate vs. time for a reversible reaction, the forward rate starts high and decreases, while the backward rate starts at zero and increases. At the point where the two curves meet: (a) Concentrations of reactants and products are equal (b) Concentrations stop changing, but rates remain equal and non-zero (c) Both reaction rates drop to zero (d) Only forward rate continues, backward rate stops

A saturated NaCl solution is at equilibrium at constant temperature. If some solid NaCl is added and stirred: (a) Concentration of Na + and Cl − increases (b) Concentration of Na + and Cl − decreases (c) Concentration remains unchanged (d) Solid NaCl dissolves completely

key: (b) Gas concentration in liquid remains constant due to equal dissolution and escape rates
stem: A sealed bottle of a carbonated drink is left unopened. Which statement about the CO 2 gas dissolved in it is correct? (a) Rate of gas escaping from liquid is greater than rate of dissolution (b) Gas concentration in liquid remains constant due to equal dissolution and escape rates (c) Dissolution stops after some time, but escape continues (d) Solubility of CO 2 increases without limit over time

A closed container at constant temperature contains liquid water and water vapour at equilibrium. A small heater is switched on, causing the vapour pressure to increase steadily until it stabilises at a new constant value. Which combination of statements is correct at the new equilibrium? 1. Rate of evaporation equals rate of condensation. 2. Number of vapour molecules striking the surface per second is greater than before heating. 3. Concentration of liquid water molecules in the container has increased. (a) 1 and 2 only (b) 1 and 3 only (c) 2 and 3 only (d) 1, 2 and 3

key: (a) R s rises sharply, then the curves meet at a higher constant value
stem: Initially, only solid iodine is placed in an evacuated container at 25 °C. Vapour pressure rises until equilibrium is established. If the temperature is suddenly increased to 35 °C, which curve correctly represents the rate of sublimation (R s ) and rate of condensation (R c ) over time? (a) R s increases sharply, then falls to meet R c at a higher constant value (b) R s decreases sharply, then rises to meet R c at a higher constant value (c) R c increases sharply, then falls to meet R s at a lower constant value (d) R c decreases steadily, meeting R s at a lower constant value

key: (c) Forward and backward rates are equal but [B] > [A]
stem: A reversible reaction A ⇌ B is studied at constant temperature. At equilibrium, [B] is double that of [A]. Which statement is correct if the rates of forward and backward reactions are plotted over time? (a) Both rates are zero at equilibrium because concentrations are constant (b) Forward rate is twice backward rate at equilibrium (c) Forward and backward rates are equal but [B] > [A] (d) Forward rate starts lower and increases until it equals backward rate

A saturated NaCl solution at 25 °C is in equilibrium with undissolved NaCl. If some water is evaporated and the temperature kept constant, which sequence correctly describes the changes? 1. Ion concentration temporarily increases. 2. Crystallisation rate becomes greater than dissolution rate. 3. Excess solid NaCl precipitates until rates are equal again. (a) 1 → 3 → 2 (b) 1 → 2 → 3 (c) 2 → 1 → 3 (d) 3 → 1 → 2

In a sealed bottle of carbonated water at equilibrium, the partial pressure of CO 2 above the liquid is 3 atm. If the bottle is opened and resealed quickly, the partial pressure drops to 1 atm. Which changes occur immediately after resealing? 1. Rate of CO 2 escape from liquid exceeds dissolution rate. 2. Concentration of dissolved CO 2 decreases until equilibrium is restored. 3. At new equilibrium, both rates are zero. (a) 1 and 2 only (b) 2 and 3 only (c) 1 and 3 only (d) 1, 2 and 3
If a system is at equilibrium the rate of forward to the reverse reaction is (a) Less (b) Equal (c) High (d) At equilibrium

Which type of equilibrium is represented by the decomposition of calcium carbonate? CaCO 3 (s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO 2 (g) (a) Homogeneous equilibrium (b) Phase equilibrium (c) Heterogeneous equilibrium (d) Aqueous equilibrium
The state in which two opposing chemical reactions continue but the net change is zero is the state of (a) oxidation (b) reduction (c) complete ionization (d) equilibrium
A reversible reaction is one which: (a) proceeds in one direction (b) proceeds in both directions (c) proceeds spontaneously (d) all the statements are wrong

key: (b) The rates of forward and backward reactions are equal
stem: A chemical reaction is at equilibrium when (a) Reactants are completely transformed into products (b) The rates of forward and backward reactions are equal (c) Formation of products is minimized (d) Equal amounts of reactants and products are present

key: (c) the graph whose two curves converge and merge at one common constant rate
stem: Which graph will show equilibrium condition? (Rate vs Time) (a) two curves that flatten out at two different rate values (b) two curves that cross and then separate to two different constant values (c) two curves — one falling, one rising — that converge and merge at one common constant rate (d) None of these

For the reaction R ⇌ P, variation of concentration is plotted against time. The plot is divided into region III (early, both curves changing steeply), region II (curves still approaching each other) and region I (beyond the dashed line, both curves flat). Which of the following regions show(s) equilibrium? (a) I (b) II (c) III (d) Both II and III

Which situation necessarily requires a closed vessel to establish equilibrium? (a) Dissolution of sugar in water (b) Fusion of ice at melting point (c) Liquid–vapour equilibrium of water (d) Solid–liquid equilibrium of camphor

A reaction mixture contains reactants and products in the same physical state and has attained equilibrium. This equilibrium is best classified as: (a) Physical equilibrium (b) Heterogeneous equilibrium (c) Homogeneous equilibrium (d) Irreversible equilibrium

Identify the type of equilibrium for the following reaction: CO(g) + H 2 O(g) ⇌ CO 2 (g) + H 2 (g) (a) Physical equilibrium (b) Homogeneous equilibrium (c) Heterogeneous equilibrium (d) Static equilibrium

key: (c) Velocity of mutual reactions become equal
stem: In any chemical reaction, equilibrium is supposed to be established when (a) Mutual opposite reactions undergo (b) Concentration of reactants and resulting products are equal (c) Velocity of mutual reactions become equal (d) The temperature of mutual opposite reactions become equal

key: (d) Both forward and backward reactions occur at all times with same speed
stem: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic in nature because (a) Equilibrium is maintained rapidly (b) The concentration of reactants and products become same at equilibrium (c) The concentration of reactants and products are constant but different (d) Both forward and backward reactions occur at all times with same speed

key: (b) Because there is a boundary between the solid iodine and the gaseous iodine
stem: Why is the equilibrium I 2 (s) ⇌ I 2 (g) considered heterogeneous? (a) Because it is a physical change, not a chemical one (b) Because there is a boundary between the solid iodine and the gaseous iodine (c) Because I 2 is a diatomic molecule (d) Because it only involves one substance

key: (c) At equilibrium only products are present
stem: Which one is not correct for a reversible reaction? (a) The reaction is never completed (b) The reactants are present in the initial stage but after that the reactants and products are always present in the reaction mixture (c) At equilibrium only products are present (d) When the reaction is carried out in closed space, it attains equilibrium state after suitable time

key: (b) a continual change between reaction components
stem: A reaction in chemical equilibrium is characterized by (a) equal concentration of reaction components (b) a continual change between reaction components (c) much greater equilibrium concentrations than initial concentrations (d) its resistance to change
Consider the following system: Ni(s) + 4CO(g) ⇌ Ni(CO) 4 (g). How many phases are present at equilibrium? (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 1 (d) 4

A reaction mixture contains both reactants and products, and their concentrations do not change with time. Which conclusion is most appropriate? (a) The reaction is irreversible (b) The reaction has stopped (c) The system is at equilibrium (d) The system is kinetically inactive

In a closed container, liquid water is in equilibrium with its vapor. If you add a salt that does not evaporate, what happens to the type of equilibrium? (a) It remains a heterogeneous equilibrium (b) It becomes a solid–gas equilibrium (c) It becomes a homogeneous equilibrium (d) The equilibrium is destroyed

The following reaction is at equilibrium: CH 3 COOCH 3 (l) + H 2 O(l) ⇌ CH 3 COOH(l) + CH 3 OH(l). If all these liquids are completely miscible, the equilibrium is: (a) Multiphase (b) Static (c) Homogeneous (d) Heterogeneous

key: (c) All the physical processes stop at equilibrium
stem: Which of the following is not a general characteristic of equilibria involving physical processes? (a) Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature (b) All measurable properties of the system remain constant (c) All the physical processes stop at equilibrium (d) The opposing processes occur at the same rate and there is dynamic but stable condition

The gaseous reaction A(g) + nB(g) ⇌ mC(g) is represented by the following curves: [B] falls from 10 M to a constant 8 M, [A] falls from 8 M to a constant 6 M, and [C] rises from 0 M to a constant 6 M. What is the value of n + m?

key: (b) Few drops of water present along with air in a balloon at constant temperature
stem: Which of the following conditions represents an equilibrium? (a) Freezing of ice in an open vessel, temperature of ice is constant (b) Few drops of water is present along with air in a balloon, temperature of balloon is constant (c) Water is boiling in an open vessel over stove, temperature of water is constant (d) All the statements A, B and C are correct for the equilibrium

key: (d) The same amount of ammonia is formed as is decomposed into N 2 and H 2
stem: In the chemical reaction N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 at equilibrium point, state whether (a) Equal volumes of N 2 and H 2 are reacting (b) Equal masses of N 2 and H 2 are reacting (c) The reaction has stopped (d) The same amount of ammonia is formed as is decomposed into N 2 and H 2

key: (d) It is heterogeneous because it contains both solid and gaseous phases
stem: Identify the ‘trick’ element in this reaction classification: 3Fe(s) + 4H 2 O(g) ⇌ Fe 3 O 4 (s) + 4H 2 (g) (a) It is heterogeneous because it is a redox reaction (b) It is homogeneous because the number of moles of gas is equal on both sides (c) It is homogeneous because the solids ‘cancel out’ in the K expression (d) It is heterogeneous because it contains both solid and gaseous phases

key: (a) Because water acts as a pure solvent and the system exists as a single liquid solution phase
stem: In the reaction NH 3 (aq) + H 2 O(l) ⇌ NH 4 + (aq) + OH − (aq), why is this considered a homogeneous equilibrium despite the ‘l’ and ‘aq’ symbols? (a) Because water acts as a pure solvent and the system exists as a single liquid solution phase (b) Because the concentration of water is ignored in the K c expression (c) Because all reactants are eventually converted to gases (d) It is actually a heterogeneous equilibrium

key: (a) Both statements correct and II is the correct explanation of I
stem: Statement I: A net reaction can occur only if a system is not at equilibrium. Statement II: All reactions occur to reach a state of equilibrium. (a) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I (b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I (c) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect (d) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

key: (a), (c), (d) observable properties constant; no net macroscopic change; opposing processes at equal rates
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] Which of the following statements are true for a system at equilibrium? (a) Observable properties of the system remain constant (b) Forward and backward reactions stop completely (c) The system shows no net macroscopic change (d) Opposing processes continue at the same rate

key: (a), (c) ice and water at the melting point in a closed system; solid iodine and its vapour in a closed container
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] Which of the following situation(s) can represent physical equilibrium? (a) Ice and water coexisting at melting point in a closed system (b) Water evaporating continuously in an open vessel (c) Solid iodine and iodine vapour in a closed container (d) Gas escaping continuously from a solution kept open

key: (a), (c), (d) proceed only in the forward direction; can proceed to completion; never attain equilibrium
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] Which of the following statements are correct about irreversible reactions? (a) They proceed only in the forward direction (b) They can be started from either reactant or product side (c) They can proceed to completion (d) They never attain equilibrium

key: (b), (d) forward and backward reactions continue simultaneously; opposing processes occur at equal rates ⚠
stem: [One or more than one option may be correct] Which observation(s) support the dynamic nature of equilibrium? (a) Observable properties of the system remain constant (b) Forward and backward reactions continue simultaneously (c) Reaction stops after equilibrium is reached (d) Opposing processes occur at equal rates
